root_cause: calc.py:average divides sum(values) by len(values) with no empty-input guard, so an empty list raises ZeroDivisionError instead of the required 0.0.
rationale: SPEC.md requires calc.average to return 0.0 for an empty list. The report states that in version 2.3 average([]) returned 0.0 and that after the upgrade to 2.4 it raises ZeroDivisionError, which is concrete prior-working evidence.
